title: Optics
description: Optics develops a rigorous understanding of light as rays, waves, electromagnetic fields, beams, photons, and engineered signals. The course integrates classical optics, photonics, imaging, lasers, nonlinear optics, guided-wave systems, optical communications, sensing, quantum optics, and laboratory design.

topics.title: Optical Field Foundations and Electromagnetic Waves
topics.description: Students ground optics in Maxwell's equations, wave propagation, energy flow, and the physical meaning of optical fields.

children.title: Maxwell-to-waves connection
children.description: The point is to see optics as an electromagnetic wave theory with measurable fields.

children.title: Energy and momentum
children.description: Students learn what optical power, intensity, and momentum mean physically.

children.title: Material response
children.description: Optical behavior depends on how matter polarizes in response to fields.

topics.title: Geometrical Optics and Imaging Systems
topics.description: This module treats light as rays to analyze lenses, mirrors, imaging, stops, pupils, and first-order optical systems.

children.title: Ray tracing
children.description: Ray methods give fast, practical tools for designing first-order systems.

children.title: Lenses and mirrors
children.description: Students analyze image formation with standard optical elements.

children.title: System layout
children.description: Imaging systems depend on stops, pupils, fields, and magnification.

topics.title: Optical Design, Aberrations, and Instrumentation
topics.description: Students learn why real systems depart from paraxial ideal behavior and how optical instruments are designed, aligned, and evaluated.

children.title: Aberrations
children.description: Students learn why real images blur even when ray optics predicts a perfect focus.

children.title: Optical instruments
children.description: Instrumentation examples connect theory to cameras, microscopes, telescopes, and spectrometers.

children.title: Design practice
children.description: Optical design requires tolerances, alignment, and measurable performance criteria.

topics.title: Wave Propagation, Gaussian Beams, and Resonators
topics.description: This topic develops beam propagation, Gaussian modes, cavity stability, and resonator behavior that are essential for lasers and photonics.

children.title: Gaussian beams
children.description: Many laser beams are best modeled by Gaussian beam propagation.

children.title: ABCD matrices
children.description: Matrix methods simplify propagation through paraxial optical systems.

children.title: Resonators
children.description: Optical cavities select modes and shape laser output.

topics.title: Interference, Coherence, and Interferometry
topics.description: Students study how phase relationships create measurable intensity patterns and enable precision measurement.

children.title: Two-beam interference
children.description: Students learn how phase differences become intensity fringes.

children.title: Coherence
children.description: Coherence determines whether interference survives real source bandwidth and size.

children.title: Precision measurement
children.description: Interferometry turns small length or phase changes into measurable signals.

topics.title: Diffraction, Apertures, and Resolution
topics.description: This module explains how finite apertures shape light, limit imaging resolution, and define the point-spread function.

children.title: Diffraction regimes
children.description: Propagation from finite apertures produces predictable spreading and structure.

children.title: Aperture functions
children.description: Aperture shape controls optical response.

children.title: Resolution limits
children.description: Diffraction sets fundamental limits on imaging and focusing.

topics.title: Fourier Optics and Computational Imaging
topics.description: Students learn how lenses, propagation, and apertures manipulate spatial frequency content and enable modern imaging methods.

children.title: Spatial frequency
children.description: Images can be understood as combinations of spatial-frequency components.

children.title: Lenses as Fourier processors
children.description: A lens can physically perform Fourier-transform operations under the right conditions.

children.title: Computational imaging
children.description: Modern imaging combines optics, sensors, and algorithms.

children.title: Synthetic aperture and coded imaging preview

topics.title: Polarization, Birefringence, and Anisotropic Media
topics.description: This topic covers the vector nature of light and how materials and optical elements transform polarization states.

children.title: Polarization states
children.description: Polarization describes the vector orientation and phase of the optical field.

children.title: Polarization optics
children.description: Optical elements can analyze or transform polarization.

children.title: Anisotropic media
children.description: Birefringent materials split and retard polarization components.

topics.title: Lasers, Optical Sources, and Photodetectors
topics.description: Students connect gain, resonators, source coherence, detector physics, and noise to practical optical systems.

children.title: Laser physics
children.description: Lasers arise from gain, feedback, and population inversion.

children.title: Optical sources
children.description: Different sources have different spectra, coherence, power, and modulation properties.

children.title: Photodetection
children.description: Detectors convert photons into electrical signals with noise and bandwidth limits.

topics.title: Nonlinear Optics and Light-Matter Interaction
topics.description: This module introduces intensity-dependent optical response, frequency conversion, ultrafast effects, and modern nonlinear applications.

children.title: Nonlinear susceptibility
children.description: At high intensity, material response can depend nonlinearly on field strength.

children.title: Frequency conversion
children.description: Nonlinear media can create new optical frequencies.

children.title: Ultrafast and nonlinear effects
children.description: Short pulses and high intensities reveal rich light-matter dynamics.

topics.title: Fiber Optics, Waveguides, and Integrated Photonics
topics.description: Students study guided-wave optics from optical fibers through silicon photonics and chip-scale devices.

children.title: Guided modes
children.description: Waveguides confine light and determine modal propagation.

children.title: Fiber optics
children.description: Fibers enable low-loss long-distance transmission and sensing.

children.title: Integrated photonics
children.description: Chip-scale optics brings waveguides, resonators, modulators, and detectors together.

topics.title: Optical Communications, Sensing, and Photonic Systems
topics.description: This topic applies optics to links, modulation, link budgets, sensing, microscopy, spectroscopy, and measurement systems.

children.title: Optical links
children.description: Communications systems require source, fiber, modulator, detector, and noise budgets.

children.title: Optical sensing
children.description: Optics can measure displacement, strain, fields, chemistry, and biological signals.

children.title: Imaging and spectroscopy systems
children.description: Photonics supports measurement across science and engineering.

topics.title: Quantum Optics and Modern Photonic Frontiers
topics.description: Students see how photons, quantum states, entanglement, and photon statistics extend classical optics into modern research.

children.title: Photon statistics
children.description: Quantum optics treats light as quantum states as well as waves.

children.title: Quantum photonic devices
children.description: Devices generate, manipulate, and detect quantum optical states.

children.title: Frontier applications
children.description: Modern optics connects to quantum information, precision metrology, and integrated systems.

topics.title: Optical Laboratory, Measurement, and Design Project
topics.description: The course closes by integrating experimental alignment, uncertainty, safety, design, simulation, and communication in a capstone optical system.

children.title: Lab practice and safety
children.description: Optics training requires careful alignment and safe handling of sources and components.

children.title: Measurement and uncertainty
children.description: Students learn to trust results by quantifying errors and repeatability.

children.title: Design project
children.description: The project integrates theory, simulation, experiment, and communication.
